articles.title_zh: Two Chinese Nationals Receive Less Than Three Years Prison Time for Spying on US Navy
articles.content_orig:
The pair was accused of gathering information about U.S. military personnel and facilitating secret cash payments.
Two Chinese nationals have been sentenced to 30 months in prison for acting as illegal agents of the People’s Republic of China after conducting surveillance operations targeting U.S. Navy personnel and military facilities.
Their charges are conspiring to act as agents of the PRC government and acting as agents of a foreign government without prior notification to the Attorney General.
One of the convicted criminals, Liren “Ryan” Lai, was arrested in Houston last year.
According to court documents, Lai and co-defendant Yuance Chen of Oregon began acting as agents under a Chinese intelligence officer with PRC’s Ministry of State Security in 2021.
Authorities alleged that the pair photographed U.S. military personnel and facilities, Navy recruiting offices, and naval installations in Washington and California.
They also reportedly attempted to recruit other potential MSS members from the U.S. military.
“Chen and Lai operated as illegal agents for the Chinese government on U.S. soil, carrying out clandestine intelligence work that included making covert payments, collecting sensitive military information, and attempting to recruit American service members,” said Assistant Director Roman Rozhavsky of the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division.
Their activities included secret “dead drop” cash payments in exchange for intelligence related to the national security of the U.S.
A dead drop of $10,000 was reportedly sent to Chen. The MSS also directed Lai to travel to Phoenix in 2025 to facilitate a cash payment of $20,000.
An unsealed federal affidavit cited an incident that involved Chen surveilling the Naval Special Warfare Command in San Diego, which oversees Navy SEALs.
The pair were arrested on June 27, 2025, in a coordinated FBI counterintelligence and law enforcement operation.
A federal grand jury in the Northern District of California returned an indictment charging both defendants with conspiracy to act as agents of a foreign government without prior notification to the attorney general and acting as agents of a foreign government without prior notification.
Both pleaded guilty and received sentences of 30 months in prison and three years of supervised release.
“Lai’s and Chen’s activities, undertaken at the direction of the PRC, were extensive and brazen. The National Security Division is committed to holding accountable anyone who aids or abets such espionage efforts,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg.
Rozhavsky noted that while “The Chinese government’s efforts to infiltrate our armed forces demonstrate just how far it will go to threaten U.S. national security,” the country has “underestimated the FBI’s commitment to thwarting its illegal activity and holding its agents accountable.”
“Let this sentencing serve as a clear warning: If you attempt to jeopardize the safety and security of our service members, our citizens, or our nation, justice will find you,” added Rozhavsky.

articles.title_zh: Review: Stellar Blade: Complete Edition (Switch 2) - Perfectly Playable, Despite Drawbacks
articles.content_orig:
Though the genre has evolved and deepened over time, gacha games have historically not been praised for their depth and complexity, often being criticised for being thinly veiled gambling machines. People were understandably incredulous, then, when Shift Up — the studio behind Goddess of Victory: Nikke — announced in 2019 that it would pursue a AAA passion project called Stellar Blade . Even more were then shocked a few years later when this wildly different, ambitious project turned out to be a pretty solidly made action game.
Stellar Blade has now been ported to Switch 2 (along with some cheeky new cosmetic Bayonetta DLC), bringing this titillating and gripping action experience to the Nintendo audience. It hasn’t made the transition to more modest hardware completely unscathed, but this is nonetheless a solidly enjoyable and thrilling adventure that deserves a spot in your library.
The narrative is set in the distant, post-apocalypse future, when our planet has been overrun by monstrous creatures called Naytibas. Some humans escaped after losing the war and established a space-based orbital colony called…the Colony…from which occasional squadrons of elite super-soldiers are deployed to attempt to regain a foothold on Earth.
Protagonist Eve is a member of one of these squads and the prologue opens with her landing mission, a violent meatgrinder reminiscent of the Omaha Beach scene in Saving Private Ryan in which she’s seemingly the sole warrior who survives. Aided by a mysterious man who saved her, Eve sets out to track down the Alpha Naytiba and hopefully notch a win for the humans.
It’s a decently entertaining story, but one which feels a little surface-level in many ways. Characters — Eve included — lack depth and converse in a stilted way that sounds as if they’re quoting lines at each other, and some of the later plot twists are the sort of thing that you can see coming a mile away. Yet there’s just enough lore here to keep you interested in the setting and Eve’s ongoing journey and occasional moments of levity help to keep things from feeling too dour.
Any disappointment with the storytelling is quickly forgotten by the thrill of combat, which feels like a cross between a Soulslike and a character action game as Eve deftly combos enemies with her athletic acrobatics and expert sword strikes.
Enemies hit hard and fast and can easily stunlock you, meaning that even a single average foe can take quite a large chunk out of your health bar if you're not paying careful attention and multiple foes at once can rapidly overwhelm Eve due to limited mobility and crowd control options.
Along with the usual combos you can string together with light and heavy attacks, Eve also has a variety of limited-use Beta Skills she can use to turn the tide in her favour. You build up Beta Energy from attacks and perfectly timed blocks or parries, and this energy can then be burned mid-combo to either bolster an attack or use a flashy guard-breaking attack that can put the enemy on the back foot. This system adds a nice bit of room for player skill expression, as you can find some creative ways to weave together combos and Beta Skills to positively melt foes.
Though even common enemies can put you to the test in certain configurations, this combat system really sings when you get to one of the many cinematic boss fights against powerful, grotesque monsters. These act as occasional hard skill checks that will forcibly teach you deeper knowledge of combat mechanics as you carefully study their movesets for brief gaps and learn (often across multiple failed attempts) how to best exploit those gaps with your available tools.
Eve thus feels both all-powerful and vulnerable at the same time, which lends combat encounters a thrilling and electric feel as you oscillate between slicing enemies to ribbons with practised cinematic flair and getting absolutely folded when you mis-time a dodge. Practice makes perfect, and there's lots of satisfaction that comes from progressing across the hours and going up against increasingly more complicated and dangerous foes with sharpened reflexes and skill.
Yet progress happens in more ways than just raw skill development - there are also some light RPG elements that allow you to slowly shape Eve's build over time. Not only can you use skill points to unlock and power up new combat abilities and Beta Skills, but you can also improve stats like max health and attack through finding collectibles in the environment.
Gear can also be found and crafted to give Eve certain passive buffs, allowing you to get more value out of the playstyle you generally choose. These RPG mechanics help to soften some of the harder edges of the often unforgiving combat system, giving you meaningful ways to progress over time even if you struggle greatly with losing battles to enemies.
World and level design initially follows traditional Soulslike tropes, consisting of lots of claustrophobic halls and labyrinthine paths that often loop back on each other with unlocked doors and ladders that lead back to the nearest checkpoint. While the critical path is usually obvious and easy to follow, there are often a handful of side areas to explore along the way rife with more platforming gauntlets, challenging enemy placements and extra upgrades and goodies. This design does a great job of rewarding exploration while keeping you moving forward.
Then, roughly six or so hours in, things change up with the sudden introduction of a medium-sized open-world area, filled with quests, collectibles, and points of interest to scour. Travelling between this area and a nearby hub has both gameplay and narrative benefits, as you complete quests and bounties to progress various side storylines for NPCs living there and find increasingly better gear and unlockables as quest and exploration rewards.
It admittedly seems at first like a weird left turn after the opening hours set very different expectations, but ultimately feels like a worthy addition to the gameplay loop. And even after its introduction, there are plenty of returns to the more focused and level-based Soulslike design, which balances out the free but occasionally meandering levels and quests that can come with the open world.
Graphics look decent, but not exceptional, due in part to both the overall art direction and the Switch 2’s relatively modest hardware. Some of the vistas of the ruined Earth can be quite nice to look at from afar, but there’s a lot of muted colours utilised as you trawl through tunnels, sewers, deserts, and destroyed office buildings. Environments thus tend to blend together and often lack visually interesting landmarks or set pieces, which can make the sections more focused on exploration a little more dull.
Meanwhile, the game outputs at 720p handheld and 1080p docked, which can lead to visuals that look even more muddy due to the upscaling artifacting and relatively low internal resolutions.
Regarding performance, everything technically runs at 60fps, but there's a pretty massive caveat with that claim: this frame rate is only accomplished through frame generation. Practically speaking, this means that there's a significant amount of input lag despite the visuals themselves appearing to animate smoothly. For a game this focused on quick reaction times and granular movement, that input lag can be a death knell and does noticeably reduce the playability of this port.
However, there is an option in the settings to turn this off and reduce the game to what appears to be closer to 40fps, which feels like a much more acceptable compromise. Controls are quite a bit more responsive here, while the frame rate is noticeably smoother than 30fps. There are some drops that can still happen when panning the camera around in larger areas, but it doesn’t overly affect the playability of combat encounters and this becomes less of an issue in the many smaller environments.

articles.title_zh: US petrol prices dip ahead of midterms as voters eye costs
articles.content_orig:
Petrol prices have dipped amid renewed diplomatic efforts to end the US-Israel war on Iran, but remain high ahead of the United States midterm elections , as the cost of living remains a central issue for voters.
On Monday, the average price for a gallon (3.78 litres) of regular petrol was $4.17, according to the American Automobile Association (AAA), which tracks daily petrol prices. That is down 12 cents from this time last week and 23 cents from a month ago.
By comparison, prices were $3.04 this time a year ago and $2.98 on February 28, when the US and Israel first struck Iran.
Diesel fuel prices remain high at $6.29 per gallon, but that is down 6 cents from this time last week. Diesel prices climbed above $6 a gallon for the first time in September before topping out at $6.53.
The average petrol price of President Donald Trump’s second term to date was set to exceed $3.46 a gallon on Monday, surpassing the previous record for a presidential administration set under former President Joe Biden, according to a Financial Times analysis of federal data.
Oil prices are continuing to fall, down 6 percent on Monday as diplomatic efforts to end the US-Israel war on Iran continued following in-person talks in Qatar over the weekend.
“Oil markets down significantly this morning after Trump signalled he favoured negotiations and not new attacks on Iran,” Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy, said in a post on X. “Oil down [approximately] 5%, wholesale gasoline and diesel pointing to roughly 16 [cents per gallon] decline. The national average could fall under $4 a gallon in the next week barring a course change.”
Cost-of-living issues remain top of mind for US voters as they head to the polls. An Associated Press-NORC poll last month found that a majority of Americans believe addressing cost-of-living issues should be a priority for Congress, including 78 percent of Republicans and 89 percent of Democrats.
“Once this conflict comes to an end, gas prices will drop drastically, and the Iranian terrorist regime will not have a nuclear weapon,” White House spokesperson Taylor Rogers told Al Jazeera. “Protecting America’s national security from threats by a radical terrorist regime that has chanted ‘Death to America’ for 47 years was the right thing to do – and President Trump is the only president who has had the courage to do it.”
Rogers added, “Thanks to the exceptional work of the US military, more oil is now flowing out of the Persian Gulf than before the Iran conflict began.”
On Wall Street, oil and gas giant stocks were trending downward in midday trading. ConocoPhillips was down 3.7 percent, Chevron 2.3 percent and ExxonMobil 3.3 percent.
The major US indices more broadly were in positive territory. The Nasdaq was up 0.7 percent, the S&P 500 0.6 percent and the Dow Jones Industrial Average 1 percent.

Hello, this is Leonie Kidd with today's edition of Morning Squawk.
Markets are ready to turn over a new leaf in November, with futures higher after closing out a tough October.
This week brings a raft of market moments, with more Magnificent Seven earnings, the midterms, and a payrolls data day on Friday.

articles.content_orig:
Marvell Technology Chairman and CEO Matt Murphy and Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston detail their record-breaking merger and how their ‘shared vision’ will create a category leader in AI connectivity on ‘The Claman Countdown.’
Marvell Technology chairman and CEO Matt Murphy said the chipmaker’s historic $115 billion acquisition of Lumentum is a "once in a generation’ opportunity to unite two of the most dominating companies in the AI boom and create a "category leader."
Appearing alongside Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston on "The Claman Countdown," Murphy detailed the companies’ record-breaking merger on Monday, predicting that the transaction will cement Marvell’s position at the forefront of AI connectivity.
"It's very rare that you can find two companies of the caliber of Lumentum and Marvell that are number one in their respective areas that find a moment in time where you can combine and create a category leader in a new category," he told anchor Liz Claman.
AMERICA AND CHINA ARE FIGHTING FOR THE FUTURE OF AI — CHIPS ARE THE BATTLEFIELD
The race to build AI infrastructure is accelerating as concerns grow over centralized technological power. (Noah Berger / Getty Images)
"This AI connectivity is going to be as consequential as… the compute category, or the memory category, the fab category, and the IP licensing category."
Murphy's comments follow the announcement of Marvell’s agreement to acquire Lumentum in a landmark $115 billion transaction, marking the largest merger between two publicly traded companies. The deal will unite two massive AI enablers, equipped with electrical and optical expertise, to address connectivity requirements for next-generation AI infrastructure .
MASSIVE AI BOOM PUTS ONE OF AMERICA’S OLDEST MANUFACTURERS ON PATH TO DOUBLE IN SIZE, CEO SAYS
"Both companies.are executing phenomenally well. And what we see, Liz, is a multiplying effect, where we're gonna do much better together in two years than we would on a standalone basis," Hurlston predicted.
Under the terms of the all-stock agreement, Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 shares of Marvell common stock for each share held, according to Marvell’s announcement.
"It’s really a historic day for the two companies," Murphy said. "We're putting together basically the best-in-class leader in AI connectivity technology for semiconductors with the leader in photonics. And it is something that hasn't been done before."
Marvell Technology Chairman and CEO Matt Murphy (Right) appeared alongside Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston (Left) on "The Claman Countdown" on Monday. (Left (Takaaki Iwabu/Bloomberg via Getty Images), Right (Lam Yik Fei/Bloomberg via Getty Images) / Getty Images)
Marvell designs artificial intelligence chips and technology that powers data centers , while Lumentum designs lasers and other optical components that use light to transmit data between chips and servers.
Murphy said Lumentum and Marvell, both headquartered in Northern California, have a "shared vision" and detailed how he believes the two tech companies will work better together than apart.
IT TOOK 3 MONTHS TO GET INSIDE THIS MASSIVE TEXAS DATA CENTER — HERE’S WHAT WE SAW
"Together, because of the additional opportunity we see with each other, there's an opportunity to really outperform as a combined company," the Marvell CEO said.
Murphy, who said the merger has received "tremendous support" from hyperscalers, told FOX Business that he expects "significant" revenue synergies and other benefits once the companies are joined together.
AI chip giant Nvidia is a strategic investor in both Lumentum, which has a market value of around $76 billion, and Marvell, with a value of roughly $172 billion.
The Marvell-Lumentum deal has garnered "super positive" feedback from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Hurlston said. (Getty )
CLICK HERE TO GET FOX BUSINESS ON THE GO
Hurlston told FOX Business that Murphy discussed the potential Lumentum acquisition with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang early in the process, adding that reaction from Nvidia has been "super positive."
"Nvidia is invested in Marvell, Nvidia is invested in Lumentum. We think we can actually bring a lot more product to bear to Nvidia a lot more quickly in this combination," Hurlston said.

articles.title_zh: China Lays Out Four Missions Leading to a Crewed Moon Landing
articles.content_orig:
China has published a mission-by-mission schedule for landing astronauts on the Moon before 2030, about a year behind NASA's 2028 target, Ars Technica reported. It is the most detailed public account so far of the country's lunar program.
Wang Xiang presented the plan on October 31 at the 7th Manned Space Academic Conference. He is deputy chief designer of China's Manned Space Program and chief designer of its lunar exploration project.
The two-day event at Beihang University was hosted by the China Manned Space Agency. It drew more than 800 experts and scholars, BigGo Finance reported.
Slides from the presentation list these steps, according to Ars Technica:
BigGo Finance summarised the 2028 to 2030 window differently. It said Wenchang, the launch site in Hainan, will host three uncrewed lunar orbit verification missions and one crewed landing.
Three astronauts would make the trip, with two going down to the surface, Shattered reported, citing Chinese state media. The third would stay in orbit aboard Mengzhou.
China lacks a rocket as powerful as the Saturn V. So the crew ship and lander launch separately. Shattered said this lets controllers confirm the lander reached lunar orbit before the crew commits to the trip.
After docking in lunar orbit, the two astronauts move into the lander and descend. They lift off, dock with Mengzhou a second time and return to Earth in the spacecraft, BigGo Finance said.
Development is under way on the lander, a moonwalk spacesuit and a crewed lunar rover.
There is no Apollo 8 or Artemis II equivalent in this plan. In those missions, a crew flies to the Moon and returns without landing, Ars Technica noted. Mengzhou will still carry astronauts to the Tiangong space station in low-Earth orbit.
In August 2025, the China Manned Space Agency tested a high-fidelity mock-up of the 26-ton Lanyue lander near Beijing. Tethers simulated lunar gravity. On February 11, Mengzhou passed a maximum dynamic pressure abort test and splashed down safely at sea.
BigGo Finance described it as China's first at-sea recovery of a crewed spacecraft.
Mengzhou has also arrived at Wenchang for the 2027 test flight. On October 22, the agency asked Chinese institutions to propose payloads for the uncrewed Lanyue flight. Shattered reported a March 1, 2027 deadline for those proposals.
It also said no firm date has been given for the crewed mission.
Ars Technica said NASA's schedule depends on lunar landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin. A US landing could slip to 2030 or later. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman has cancelled the Lunar Gateway space station.
He has also cancelled planned upgrades to the Space Launch System rocket.
Shattered reported that Artemis III is now a crewed Earth-orbit test in 2027. The first landing moves to Artemis IV, targeted for early 2028.

articles.title_orig: China Tech Stocks Get Fresh Lifeline From Beijing
articles.title_zh: China Tech Stocks Get Fresh Lifeline From Beijing
articles.content_orig:
Alibaba BABA , JD.com JD and PDD Holdings PDD moved higher in U.S. premarket trading Monday after Chinese regulators signaled a fresh effort to stabilize the country's battered stock market.
The move follows an 8.5% October drop in the CSI 300 , its worst monthly performance since early 2016. The benchmark had also fallen for 12 consecutive weeks, according to TipRanks.
Beijing is now stepping in with more liquidity.
The People's Bank of China said it will conduct a new swap operation Tuesday that could inject more than 100 billion yuan, or roughly $15 billion , into the equity market. Thirty-one brokerages and fund companies have already applied for quotas worth more than 100 billion yuan.
The swap facility allows securities firms, insurers and fund managers to exchange eligible assets for more liquid central-bank assets, giving them additional capacity to buy stocks.
China is also making its relending program for share repurchases and stake increases a long-term mechanism , while cutting the program's interest rate to 1% from 1.25% .
Regulators are applying pressure directly as well.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission urged major index constituents and leading technology companies to actively buy back shares , while also encouraging newer ETFs and fund managers to increase equity exposure during the downturn. Officials are separately studying whether to ease margin rules to improve market liquidity.
The policy response helped lift sentiment Monday, with the Shanghai Composite gaining 1.1% and the CSI 300 also moving higher.
Alibaba, JD and PDD have been caught in the broader decline as investors grapple with weak Chinese consumption, persistent property-sector problems and pressure across technology shares.
I think the key point here is that Beijing is sending a clearer message that it does not want the equity selloff to spiral.
For Alibaba, JD and PDD, that matters because their stocks have increasingly been trading on macro sentiment and policy risk, not just company fundamentals.
The latest measures can improve liquidity and potentially put a floor under sentiment.
But they do not fix the underlying issues by themselves.
China still needs stronger consumption, better economic momentum and more confidence in corporate earnings for the rally to become durable.
For investors, the key things to watch are how much of the new liquidity is actually deployed, whether corporate buybacks accelerate, and whether China follows these market-support steps with broader fiscal or economic stimulus .
The immediate signal is supportive.
The harder question is whether Beijing can turn that support into a lasting recovery.

articles.title_orig: How China Might Target US Midterms - Center for European Policy Analysis (CEPA)
articles.title_zh: How China Might Target US Midterms - Center for European Policy Analysis (CEPA)
articles.content_orig:
No research shows Chinese propaganda or disinformation playing a pivotal role in the midterm elections, particularly when compared to Russia’s aggressive attempts. Yet significant blind spots exist. If it desired, Beijing is well-positioned to shape political debate through the WeChat app and through Chinese AI models.
Rather than shifting control of Congress, Beijing’s goal would likely be to reduce the presence of known Communist Party critics, particularly those serving in the Congressional-Executive Commission on China. Created by Congress in October 2000, the Commission monitors Chinese human rights and rule of law.
Several competitive races feature Commission members, including former Senator Sherrod Brown in Ohio and current Commission Chair Dan Sullivan in Alaska. House races in Iowa and Virginia involve current Commission members Zach Nunn and Jen Kiggans. Ashley Hinson, who is running for the Senate in Iowa, is on the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, another Congressional body critical of the regime.
Texas looks particularly sensitive for a different reason. WeChat , a messaging and multi-function app, has an estimated 1.5 million US users, concentrated in states with large Chinese American populations. Chinese Americans make up roughly one percent of Texas’s population .
Chinese state-sponsored censorship on WeChat is well-documented. A 2025 University of Texas study based on interviews with 20 Chinese Americans in Texas detailed how political misinformation circulates on the platform. One young interviewee described how her father read that an Asian American woman had been elected mayor of Boston months before the actual election.
“He just accepts everything he reads, and then he just forwards it,” she said. “My mother-in-law, too.”
Cultural and social pressures reduce willingness to correct misinformation in family or friend groups. “It doesn’t feel right for me to talk bad to my elders, especially in the group chat setting,” a 19-year-old Chinese American explained.
In this environment, the app is powerful. “A lot of people don’t know who to vote for, so they are easily swayed,” another interviewee commented. “It is a big political platform, and a lot of people will just blindly follow.”
The 2026 elections are the first to take place in an environment where AI chatbots are widely available. About one-fifth of Americans plan to use AI tools to help learn about candidates or inform voting decisions, according to a recent survey . Most will turn to American models such as ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, or Perplexity, but many US developers are increasingly relying on Chinese-origin models such as DeepSeek and Qwen, allowing them to enter the US information environment.
These models reflect the Chinese government’s official stances on domestic politics and human rights. Censorship and propaganda have also been found in responses to questions about US press freedom and elections.
One study examined Chinese AI models’ responses to questions about the upcoming US elections. Conducted by a research group based in Europe, researchers tested seven AI models (five US and two Chinese) with a set of 20 polling-style questions.
All models proved relatively consistent and offered mixed results in terms of partisan preferences. The two Chinese models did not diverge sharply from their US counterparts in their responses. DeepSeek, for example, selected the Democratic option on two questions about which party’s candidate it would select for Congress and which party it prefers to control Congress. So did Claude and Perplexity (99% on one of the questions). By contrast, Qwen chose Democrats 55% and 75% of the time, respectively.
The results are striking for what they show about the leeway allowed the Chinese models to comment on US versus Chinese politics. DeepSeek offered critical assessments of the US president’s job performance. Asking the same questions about Chinese President Xi Jinping would almost certainly produce refusals or strictly glowing reviews.
Major holes remain in our understanding of where and how Chinese Communist Party-linked electoral influence could be occurring. Researchers, election monitors, and others focused on election integrity should address these gaps — particularly before the 2028 elections.
Sarah Cook is founder of China Rights Analytics and Advising LLC and author of the UnderReported China newsletter.

articles.title_orig: 'Exceptionally horrific strike' — Russian bombs hit school used as humanitarian aid center in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, killing 26
articles.title_zh: 'Exceptionally horrific strike' — Russian bombs hit school used as humanitarian aid center in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, killing 26
articles.content_orig:
Video shows smoke rising from Komyshuvakha blast crater
At least 26 people were killed after Russian bombs hit an aid distribution centre, in an attack that Ukraine's leader has called "utterly horrific".
Five people were injured and 27 initially reported missing after at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit the village of Komyshuvakha in the southern Zaporizhzhia region, regional head Mykhailo Semikin said.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said that after the first strike on the local school "used for humanitarian needs", there was a second attack on the place where people were sheltering.
He posted a video showing a huge crater left after Monday's attack, and rescuer teams searching through the rubble.
The Russian military has not publicly commented.
There are fears that the death toll will rise further as a number of people are still under the rubble
Zelensky initially put the death toll at 18, but Ukraine's state emergencies service DSNS later said 24 people, including two rescuers and four police officers, were confirmed to have been killed.
In his video address late on Monday, Zelensky said 26 people were now known to have died.
He earlier said that "the Russians could not have been unaware that the local residents who remained in Komyshuvakha received humanitarian aid there every week" on Monday.
"This is yet another proof that Russia does not want any de-escalation."
He said that after a recent successful joint Russian-Ukrainian operation to evacuate civilians from the Russia-occupied southern city of Oleshky during a temporary ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump, "there was a moment when the next steps could show that peace is possible".
"With such killings, Russia is sending the exact opposite signal - Russia is counting on further killings," Zelensky said.
The Russian strikes left a huge crater where Ukrainian officials say people were sheltering
Meanwhile, Semikin described the Russian attack as a "terrible tragedy" for the village, confirming that "people are still under the rubble".
He said rescue teams were working at the scene, but they had been forced to halt their operation a number of times because of Russian drone attacks in the area.
A day of mourning has been declared for Tuesday across the entire Zaporizhzhia region.
Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Teams from Ukraine, Russia and the US are due to resume peace talks in the next few days after negotiations were suspended in February, with Moscow stepping up attacks as Kyiv virtually ran out of Western-supplied interceptors to defend against missiles.
However, no major breakthrough is expected at the talks that are likely to be held in Abu Dhabi, the United Arab Emirates.

articles.title_orig: Oil prices slide as hopes rise for potential US-Iran diplomatic breakthrough
articles.title_zh: Oil prices slide as hopes rise for potential US-Iran diplomatic breakthrough
articles.content_orig:
Crude oil prices fell sharply Monday as the presidents of the U.S. and Iran signalled they are open to a diplomatic solution to the conflict that has disrupted energy markets for eight months.
U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures shed 7.4% to close at $96.46 a barrel, the biggest daily loss since July 27. Brent crude , the international benchmark, lost 7.6% to settle at $104.77 a barrel.
President Donald Trump told reporters Monday that Iran wants to "make a deal and that could happen." U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said over the weekend that Trump prefers not to use military force against Iran and would like to resolve the conflict diplomatically.
Trump has previously said that he will not attack Iran before the U.S. midterms. But the oil market had priced in the risk of a major military escalation after the elections, gaining more than 10% in October.
The oil market has sold off during previous phases of the war on rumors of a possible settlement, only for the conflict to subsequently escalate and spike prices again.
Trump "hasn't made a decision" on whether to strike Iran again, Rubio told reporters.
"What the president expresses to you is incredible confidence that if we needed to do something militarily, we would have the ability to do it," the secretary of State said. "But we would prefer to do it peacefully."
Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said Tehran is seeking to resolve problems through dialogue, according to state-owned Islamic Republic News Agency . Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei has granted the government certain authorities to do this, Pezeshkian said.
Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, said an agreement with the U.S. is possible if Washington "demonstrates goodwill" and is "truly seeking a peaceful solution," according to IRNA.
Araghchi said mediators are discussing the proposal Iran made during the United Nations General Assembly in September. Tehran expects the U.S. to lift sanctions, reduce its military presence in the region to previous levels and lift the blockade, the foreign minister said.
But Khamenei on Saturday called for Tehran's armed forces to meet "any level or type of threat" with "an immediate, impactful, and geographically unrestricted response."
Reports about diplomatic efforts will have a big impact on crude oil prices because much of the market's recent gains were risk premium in anticipation of a possible escalation, according to Ryan McKay, director of commodity strategy at TD Securities.
"With that said, so long as there is no concrete conclusion to the war, and tanker and Houthi attacks remain prevalent, we do not anticipate a complete erosion of the risk premium via diplomacy headlines alone," McKay said.
— CNBC's Lim Hui Jie contributed to this report.

articles.title_zh: China Is Sending AI-Powered Robots Into the Ocean to Uncover Its Lost Ancient History
articles.content_orig:
China's next five-year archaeological plan, covering 2026 to 2030 , proposes deploying artificial intelligence, ancient-DNA analysis, remote sensing and deep-sea robots across some of the country's most significant historical sites. The program is designed to recover artifacts, reconstruct damaged objects and investigate questions about human migration, early states and maritime trade that conventional excavation has so far left only partially answered.
Excavations routinely produce large quantities of broken, scattered material whose connections are difficult to establish manually. Specialized AI systems would identify artifact fragments, match pieces to one another and generate virtual restorations , allowing researchers to study an object's probable original appearance without physically altering the surviving material.
Each pillar of the plan addresses a distinct limitation of conventional archaeological methods.
Remote sensing , which uses aerial or satellite data to detect buried structures, could help researchers locate remains before excavation begins. Ancient-DNA analysis would contribute to population research, tracing relationships, migrations and environmental adaptation among communities that lived thousands of years ago. Usable results require biological material preserved well enough to avoid contamination.
Underwater robotics addresses sites that human divers cannot safely reach. The plan calls for purpose-built deep-sea robots , specialized diving equipment and precision excavation tools aimed at shipwrecks and Maritime Silk Road routes lying on the seabed.
Institutionally, the program is intended to be permanent rather than a series of isolated projects. The official plan describes a national-level archaeological laboratory and a maritime-archaeology hub in Qingdao, signaling an effort to embed high-technology research into standing infrastructure.
Named sites and international partnerships give the blueprint a concrete geographic scope.
Research targets extend from northern China's earliest known sites through the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and across Eurasia. Among the domestic priorities is the transition from Paleolithic hunter-gatherer life to agriculture and settled communities along the Yellow River, Yangtze River and southern Lingnan region.
Major Bronze Age and early-state sites, including Sanxingdui , Erlitou and Yinxu, feature prominently alongside historical infrastructure such as the Qin dynasty Direct Road, the Great Wall and the Grand Canal. International partnerships with institutions in Egypt, Greece, Saudi Arabia and Tunisia are planned for comparative research, underwater surveys and heritage preservation.
The Nanhai No. 1 shows what underwater excavation can recover and what it demands in return.
The Nanhai No. 1 , a Southern Song-era merchant vessel associated with trade between China and overseas markets, illustrates why underwater archaeology occupies a central place in the new blueprint. Discovered in 1987 and raised intact in 2007, the wreck was transferred to a purpose-built aquatic environment at the Guangdong Maritime Silk Road Museum, where conservation and excavation continue under controlled conditions.
UNESCO describes the site as unusually valuable because its preservation captures cargo and food remains that document commerce and daily life aboard the vessel. According to a government-linked report, more than 180,000 cultural relics have been salvaged and preserved from the site.
Ambition and evidence are not the same thing, and the plan's limits deserve equal billing.
AI cannot reconstruct information the surviving evidence does not support; a virtual restoration is only as reliable as the fragments behind it. Deep-sea robots still contend with pressure, poor visibility, currents and fragile materials.
Ancient-DNA results depend on preservation conditions and rigorous contamination controls, and their interpretation requires care. None of this invalidates the program's potential, but discovery and conclusion are not the same thing.
The blueprint's stated cultural objectives are as significant as its scientific ones, and they invite scrutiny.
The plan carries an explicit cultural objective alongside its scientific aims: increasing China's international influence over interpretations of its history and civilization. That goal raises practical questions about data access, interpretive independence and the terms under which foreign institutions will participate. How those questions are answered will determine whether the international partnerships function as genuine scholarly collaboration or primarily serve a national framing agenda. Those details remain unclear and will merit close attention as the program moves from blueprint to fieldwork.

articles.title_zh: Mercedes Sales Plunge 31% in China as It Eyes Bigger US Push
articles.content_orig:
China sales fell 31% last quarter, yet Mercedes says it is “indispensable” and plans to build future Chinese-market cars almost entirely with local parts.
2027 Mercedes-Benz CLA 220 Hybrid in Manufaktur Patagonia Red
Mercedes-Benz , though currently struggling to retain market position in China, says it will give a broader 2030 strategy update, which will include a detailed review of its China business, next year. The numbers explain the urgency: German brands have been getting crushed in China .
Mercedes-Benz is doubling down on the market that is hurting it most. According to Reuters , CEO Ola Källenius calls China an “indispensable market and innovation hub.
Third-quarter Mercedes-Benz Cars sales fell 8 percent to 407,232, with China down 31 percent to 86,800, according to BigGo . Elsewhere, Europe was up 5 percent, Germany was up 13 percent, and the US was up 6 percent, with record battery-electric sales up 61 percent. Adjusted return on sales for cars dropped to 2.5 percent from 4.8 percent, and Mercedes cut its full-year guidance to 2-3 percent from 3-5 percent; its CFO called the fourth quarter “a break-even quarter.”
Starting with the electric E-Class in the second half of 2027, Källenius said Mercedes will source “almost everything” in China for Chinese production. According to reports, CFO Harald Wilhelm also wants the company to rely less on China as a profit source. That is a split-screen strategy: stay in the world’s largest car market, but with local suppliers and less exposure to its price war. Mercedes has already felt that pain from tariffs and China’s EV boom.
If you live in the US, this is the good-news part. The China sourcing applies to cars built for China, and nothing in the reporting says it changes what’s sold here. What matters more is where Mercedes is growing: US sales rose 6 percent last quarter, and Källenius said the company plans further US investments and sees potential to lift annual sales from more than 300,000 vehicles toward 400,000, per Reuters. Audi announced a $4 billion US assembly plant that will create around 4,500 jobs. Mercedes too is changing gears in a push for higher volume after years of sliding sales. For buyers, that could mean more attention and more incentives, though nothing has been promised.
In Germany, Mercedes will relaunch a voluntary severance program for indirect staff from December. It booked about €1.8 billion (about $2 billion) in provisions for the last round in 2025, with most of the new program’s earnings impact expected in 2027. Källenius said further German investment depends on productivity and costs, noting US labor costs run at roughly 80 percent of German levels.

articles.title_orig: Rivian Is Doing The Damn Thing
articles.title_zh: Rivian Is Doing The Damn Thing
articles.content_orig:
There's never a guarantee a startup car company will actually make it. Automotive history is littered with companies that never made it more than a few years, and after some of Rivian's early financial troubles, it wasn't out of the question that the Irvine, California-based company could join that group. Well, following the introduction of the R2 , those fears seem to be all but squashed.
Rivian just posted its third-quarter results for 2026, and the compact-crossover-sized R2 helped raise the automaker's deliveries by 46% year-over-year to 19,248 vehicles, according to Car and Driver . That means Rivian is increasing its yearly sales projection to between 67,000 and 70,000 vehicles — up from 65,000 to 70,000. It also just so happened to outsell the larger and more expensive R1S and R1T flagships combined, as well as the EDV delivery van. I should note that Rivian didn't explicitly say how many R2s it sold, though. This news comes even though the only R2 that Rivian currently sells is the most expensive Performance version of the electric SUV, and the idea that Rivian is still "early in the ramp" of R2 production, according to CEO RJ Scaringe, who spoke with Reuters .
Theoretically, things are only going to get better from here, sales-wise, with the only currently available R2 clocking in at $59,485, including destination. Eventually, a $55,485 Premium trim and $46,485 base model will join its ranks , but the only information we've got is "coming late 2026" and "coming spring 2027," respectively. Of course, even the most expensive R2 is a hell of a lot cheaper than the R1S and R1T, which both start well north of $80,000.
And good news keeps coming, because last week, Scaringe said he was "very confident" Rivian would hit an autonomy milestone this year that would unlock a quarter-billion-dollar tranche of investment money from Uber. That's part of an up-to $1.25 billion investment the rideshare company is making in the automaker through 2031, according to Reuters. It includes an initial $300 million and is contingent on several autonomy milestones. However, Rivian hasn't said exactly what those milestones are. Don't worry, though. Scaringe says Rivian is "right on time."
We do know that the partnership between Uber and Rivian targets the 2028 launch of a driverless R2 robotaxi on Uber's network — starting in a handful of cities and then expanding to about 25 over the next year and a half. Clearly, Rivian is aiming its R2 robotaxi directly at the Tesla Cybercab.
It needs to work, too. As Reuters points out, both the R2's success and the Uber partnership are imperative for making Rivian stick as a company. It's doing pretty well right now, don't get me wrong, but it's still burning through cash like the Bouvier Beale family, and it's looking for any way to narrow those losses.
No matter how you slice it, Rivian is truly showing it's a company that has the ability to stick around and be viable. Once R2 production is fully ramped up and the R3 is introduced, who knows where it could end up? All it needs to do is get that pesky cash burn problem under control.

articles.title_orig: Nearly Two Thousand Chinese Businesses Established in Nicaragua Since Free Trade Agreement Took Effect
articles.title_zh: Nearly Two Thousand Chinese Businesses Established in Nicaragua Since Free Trade Agreement Took Effect
articles.content_orig:
COSTA RICA'S LEADING ENGLISH LANGUAGE NEWSPAPER
Nearly 2,000 Chinese businesses have been established in Nicaragua during the first two years of the free trade agreement with China, according to the president of the Asociación Pro-Unificación Pacífica de China en Nicaragua. Shujin Huang made the statement to official media outlets after an event marking the 160th anniversary of the birth of Sun Yat-sen.
He said the association continues to promote additional investment from China, describing Nicaragua as a safe country with a competitive market. The free trade agreement between the two countries entered into force on January 1, 2024. The Banco Central de Nicaragua reported that net foreign direct investment from China reached 29.3 million dollars in 2025.
That figure represented 1.9 percent of the 1,502.5 million dollars in total net foreign direct investment recorded by the country that year. In 2024, any Chinese flows were not reported separately and would have been included in aggregate categories if present at all. Huang said the businesses operate mainly in commerce, with some also active in free-zone maquilas. The relatively low official investment total relative to the number of establishments indicates that most are small-scale operations.
The Asociación Pro-Unificación Pacífica de China en Nicaragua was founded in May 2024 and was officially registered as a legal organization under Ministerial Agreement 24-2024-OSFL, allowing it to operate in its own name under Nicaraguan law. Its founding event included participation by Chinese Ambassador Chen Xi and Nicaraguan officials including National Assembly President Gustavo Porras, Foreign Minister Denis Moncada and Presidential Adviser Laureano Ortega Murillo.
As part of the commercial expansion, construction of a Chinatown complex advances in Managua near the Rotonda Universitaria. The project, also known as Plaza China or Plaza 101, involves a two-story structure of approximately 8,000 square meters with an investment of about 3 million dollars. It is planned to house around 100 businesses operated by Chinese, other Asian and Nicaraguan owners.
The site currently holds roughly 30 businesses. Administrators have described the work as being in an intermediate phase, including installation of a stone arch more than six meters high carved in a dragon style and brought from China. The complex is intended to concentrate commercial activity, gastronomy and cultural offerings. Huang cited the existing Plaza China as an example of growing Chinese capital presence, noting that more than ten foreign-investment businesses already operate there.
Nicaragua and China restored diplomatic relations in December 2021 after Managua broke ties with Taiwan. The free trade agreement was signed on August 31, 2023. Official Nicaraguan statements have presented the pact and related initiatives as measures to expand trade and investment opportunities. The association’s stated goals include supporting Chinese investors and promoting the policy of one China.
As of now, the association continues to encourage further arrivals of Chinese capital. Construction on the Managua Chinatown project remains under way, with officials and association representatives describing it as a visible marker of the commercial presence that has developed since the trade agreement took effect. The Banco Central de Nicaragua has not published a full country-by-country breakdown beyond the 2025 net total that places China at 29.3 million dollars.

articles.title_orig: Leicestershire Reform council leader quits after staff comments leaked
articles.title_zh: Leicestershire Reform council leader quits after staff comments leaked
articles.content_orig:
The Reform UK leader of Leicestershire County Council has announced he is standing down after comments he made about staff redundancies were leaked online.
Dan Harrison announced on Monday that he would be stepping down from the role he has held since May 2025.
He said he had made the decision after taking advice from senior Reform colleagues, and added deputy council leader Kevin Crook had taken over as acting leader.
It comes after Harrison had apologised after being recorded saying 76 council solicitors would be made redundant, branding them "incompetent", before saying "what I want to look at now is the women", in remarks which were then released on social media.
In a statement, Harrison said it had been the "honour of his life" to lead the county council's first Reform administration.
Harrison has said he will remain as a councillor, representing the Ashby-de-la-Zouch division.
The Conservative opposition at County Hall had called for Harrison to resign after his comments about staff were leaked.
In the recording, Harrison said: "There's 76 solicitors will be made redundant.
"We'll buy in the service, because [they are] incompetent. They're not doing a good job.
"What I want to look at now is the women so it is ongoing, I would like it to be at great pace but I can tell you now if we suddenly drove massive redundancies the liberals would walk away."
Earlier on Monday, Harrison had told the BBC he would not be stepping down - but he later said he made his decision after talking to Crook and group whip Andrew Hamilton-Gray.
He had apologised over the remarks, which were made on Tuesday during a Reform party meeting.
Despite his apology, Harrison had insisted his remarks had been taken out of context.
Harrison said: "I would like to apologise unreservedly to the staff and officers of the county council for any hurt, distress or offence caused by the publication of these comments, which were made during a heated meeting with the expectation of privacy and confidentiality.
"However, I would like to stress that these discussions were just that, and I have not given any instruction or direction to officers in these matters and that there has not been any discussion nor agreement on these issues with officers."
He added: "I unequivocally reject any suggestion that staffing decisions are being taken based on gender.
"The comments made in that meeting were taken completely out of context."
Before Harrison's resignation, the council's 15 Tory councillors had called for an emergency vote to try to remove him from the leader's role.
Group leader of the Conservative group, Deborah Taylor, said: "That was not a decision we took lightly.
"The serious concerns raised over recent days, particularly around the treatment of council employees and the comments contained in leaked recordings, left us feeling that his position had become untenable.
"His resignation brings an end to his leadership, but it does not mean those concerns should simply be forgotten.
"There are still questions that deserve answers, and it is important that the council learns from what has happened."
The Reform group remains the largest party on the authority, and runs it as a minority administration.
In a statement, Jeevun Sandher and Amanda Hack - Labour MPs for Loughborough and North West Leicestershire respectively - said: "Since taking office in 2025, the Reform UK administration has become increasingly embroiled in controversy and scandal, rather than focusing on delivering for the residents of Leicestershire.
"This is far from an isolated incident. Just last week, councillor [Joseph] Boam was found to have breached the council's own code of conduct through his actions against the former monitoring officer, while other Reform councillors have also been forced to apologise to residents over their behaviour. All of this in less than two years.
"Leicestershire residents deserve better."

articles.title_orig: Can Pakistan Help Break China’s Critical Minerals Dominance?
articles.title_zh: Can Pakistan Help Break China’s Critical Minerals Dominance?
articles.content_orig:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio speaks with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir before meeting with President Donald Trump in the Oval Office, on September 25, 2025. Pakistan’s  mineral wealth can help break China’s hold on the global critical minerals market, writes Derek Grossman. (The White House/Daniel Torok)
China has spent decades building a near-stranglehold on critical mineral supply chains, leaving the United States dangerously dependent on its chief strategic rival. Even President Donald Trump ’s recent trade truce with Chinese leader Xi Jinping has done little to resolve the underlying problem: America’s continued dependence on Chinese processing of minerals essential to its economy and national security. But the Trump administration is aggressively challenging Beijing’s dominance across the globe, and over the past year, it has engaged an unlikely partner: Pakistan .
To be sure, Pakistan has been an important, if at times complicated, American strategic partner since the Cold War, helping Washington counter Soviet expansionism and, after the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks, supporting US military operations in Afghanistan . Bilateral ties have seen periods of strain, but Trump’s return to the White House has brought a major reboot. Since then, Trump has met multiple times with senior Pakistani leaders, including Field Marshal Asim Munir and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. Most recently, Islamabad has served as a key mediator between the United States and Iran in efforts to end their war, ushering in a remarkable revival in bilateral relations.
And now, there’s apparently a new area to explore: critical minerals. Over the past year, the Trump administration has stepped up discussions with Islamabad on developing Pakistan’s largely untapped mineral wealth, including a $500 million agreement between an American company and Pakistan’s Frontier Works Organization to cooperate on mining and processing critical minerals, including rare earths.
Washington has also backed the massive Reko Diq copper and gold project through $1.25 billion in Export-Import Bank financing , underscoring its growing interest in Pakistan as an alternative source of strategic minerals. Pakistan, meanwhile, stands to benefit economically from greater American investment in a mining sector that currently accounts for only about 3 percent of its GDP.
Last April, a US delegation led by Eric Meyer of the State Department attended the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum in Islamabad and conveyed the interest of American companies in the sector. With the forum returning November 12–13 , renewed American participation—particularly if accompanied by fresh investment commitments—would demonstrate that Washington is serious about turning its growing interest in Pakistan’s mineral wealth into a lasting strategic partnership.
Deeper US-Pakistan cooperation on critical minerals could help Washington chip away at Beijing’s dominance over global supply chains. Early American investment could also help determine where Pakistan’s minerals are processed and who ultimately purchases them, rather than allowing Beijing to lock in these arrangements before Washington has a chance to compete.
Indeed, Pakistan is just one piece of the Trump administration’s broader strategy to reduce dependence on China, with Washington pursuing critical minerals agreements and partnerships across Asia, including Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Australia, as well as resource-rich countries such as Argentina, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Ukraine.
Washington’s experience in Africa suggests the bet can pay off. The Democratic Republic of the Congo is a country where conflict in the east has complicated the operating environment and where Chinese firms have long held the advantage, yet the United States has leaned in anyway, building on a Lobito Corridor initiative that began under the Biden administration and that Trump has carried forward. In December 2025, Washington and Kinshasa signed a Strategic Partnership Agreement reportedly giving American companies a right of first offer on designated mineral deposits.
This July, the Development Finance Corporation and the Development Bank of Southern Africa closed a $753 million package to upgrade the Lobito Atlantic Railway, which carries Congolese and Zambian copper and cobalt to Angola’s Atlantic coast, and the operator now expects to double its international cargo to 800,000 tons next year .
In May, the DRC’s state cobalt entity also agreed to supply cobalt hydroxide to a US-based firm. Progress has not been linear, and the DRC’s task force for the minerals pact was set up months behind schedule, but the lesson is clear: sustained commitment in a difficult jurisdiction can reshape supply chains in ways that waiting for ideal conditions never will. Pakistan has its own challenges, but trust built through early investment is what gives American companies a seat at the table.
But challenges remain. For starters, Pakistan’s evolving domestic security situation, particularly in mineral-rich Balochistan, will shape how quickly American companies can establish an on-the-ground presence. The Barrick Mining Corporation has slowed development of the massive Reko Diq copper and gold project while it reviews the security environment in Pakistan and the wider region, though it has said it continues to believe in the project’s long-term value and has kept Phase 1 approved, a reminder that investors will need to price in risk and that Islamabad has a strong interest in improving the conditions for them.
Another constraint is that Beijing, having entered Pakistan’s mining sector much earlier, already enjoys significant advantages in infrastructure, expertise, and established commercial relationships, forcing Washington to play catch-up. According to a recent Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) report, China already purchases approximately 95 percent of Pakistan’s exported copper ores and concentrates, illustrating just how deeply Beijing is embedded in Pakistan’s existing minerals trade.
Nevertheless, the upcoming critical minerals conference, along with potential new Trump administration agreements with Islamabad, could help narrow this gap—provided they translate into concrete investments and sustained cooperation. Moreover, much of Pakistan’s critical mineral wealth remains underexplored, giving American companies a chance to help identify and develop commercially viable deposits, particularly antimony—a strategically important critical mineral used in ammunition, explosives, flame retardants, and advanced military technologies, making it essential to US defense manufacturing and national security—while potentially establishing new processing facilities outside China’s control. Islamabad also has an incentive to welcome American investment as a way to diversify its economic relationships without abandoning its longstanding strategic partnership with Beijing.
Though making that case a reality will take more than just this. Washington could start by pairing its financing with tools that help American firms manage the risks of a frontier jurisdiction, such as political risk insurance and co-financing alongside development banks and Gulf investors, so that capital can move before conditions are perfect. It should prioritize processing as much as extraction, because the real leverage lies in refining, and the opportunity to build facilities outside China’s control is greatest while Pakistan’s sector is still taking shape.
And it should treat the relationship as a durable economic partnership rather than an extension of its diplomacy around Iran, with offtake agreements and technical cooperation that give both sides a stake in the outcome. articles.title_orig: SpaceX weighs Boost Mobile deal in push for Starlink phone service: Report
articles.title_zh: SpaceX weighs Boost Mobile deal in push for Starlink phone service: Report
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
SpaceX ( SPCX ) may be attempting an end run to circumvent obstacles it's facing in getting a mobile network off the ground.
Per the Washington Post , SpaceX is in talks with EchoStar ( SATS ) about launching its own wireless phone service through Boost Mobile, after the country's three biggest carriers — Verizon, AT&T ( T ), and T-Mobile ( TMUS ) — reportedly turned down SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.
Musk met with EchoStar chairman Charlie Ergen last month, according to two people familiar with the negotiations cited by the Post. The talks could end with SpaceX buying Boost Mobile outright or getting access to its network, which the discount carrier leases from AT&T and T-Mobile.
In recent months, Musk asked the heads of Verizon ( VZ ), AT&T and T-Mobile to let SpaceX use their networks for its own mobile service. All three said no, per the Post.
But there may be a catch to SpaceX's plan. Typically, a carrier's lease agreement can't be transferred to a new owner without the host carrier's permission, meaning AT&T and T-Mobile may still need to approve a Boost deal to provide access to SpaceX.
SpaceX is open about its ambitions in the terrestrial mobile space. On the company's recent earnings call , CFO Bret Johnsen said the goal is to "become a major mobile carrier ... in the United States." SpaceX also recently agreed to buy $8 billion worth of wireless spectrum licenses intended for cellular service in places satellites can't reach.
"This is the last critical piece of the spectrum puzzle needed for SpaceX to provide complete phone coverage in America," Musk said on X .
SpaceX and EchoStar already have a relationship. In September 2025, SpaceX agreed to buy EchoStar's AWS-4 and H-block spectrum licenses for about $17 billion, split between up to $8.5 billion in cash and up to $8.5 billion in SpaceX stock, EchoStar said at the time . SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell said the deal would "advance our mission to end mobile dead zones."
What SpaceX still lacks is a ground network. Its satellite signal isn't strong enough yet to carry cell coverage indoors or in dense cities, where most phones are - and that's why a deal with Boost would be so crucial.
An MVNO (mobile virtual network operator) like Boost rents capacity on an existing carrier's network. Last month, TD Cowen's Gregory Williams called acquiring an MVNO the cheapest and fastest route for SpaceX to launch mobile service, noting a network build would cost "upwards of $80B" and take years.
The Big 3, he said, still show no desire "to (ever) sign an MVNO deal with Starlink that could ravage the industry."
Carrier executives have publicly doubted that SpaceX can rebuild their tower networks. Verizon's CEO put the build-out at four to six years. Musk said it would take about half that.
"Veterans of the cellular industry look at the chess board of existing pieces and don't see a solution," Musk said recently on X . "They don't understand that SpaceX is developing entirely new pieces that fundamentally alter the strategic landscape."

articles.title_orig: China’s AI Data Centers Move West, But Their Tax Revenue Stays East - The Diplomat
articles.title_zh: China’s AI Data Centers Move West, But Their Tax Revenue Stays East - The Diplomat
articles.content_orig:
When Chinese President Xi Jinping visited Ulanqab in Inner Mongolia in mid-October, he was briefed on its computing industry and called for efforts to “extend the industrial chain” and keep “transforming the strength in computing into development advantages.” Ulanqab is cold, electricity is cheap, and Beijing is close , so the city became a hub of the data-center boom powering China’s AI race with the United States. Yet a city official told the Economic Observer that the industry is still “losing money” and that tax revenue will build up gradually only once projects under construction start operating.
After the data centers open, however, the companies selling cloud services and AI models pay the tax on those sales in Hangzhou and Beijing, where they are registered. Most of the tax that stays in Ulanqab is paid during construction. If nothing changes, Ulanqab will struggle to turn its computing advantage into a development advantage of its own.
In China, where tax is paid depends on where the invoicing company is registered. Both value-added tax (VAT) and corporate income tax are paid there , and the local government keeps half of the VAT and 40 percent of the corporate income tax . If you rent a server on Alibaba Cloud, you can choose a data center in Ulanqab, but the invoice comes from the company registered in Hangzhou.
Alibaba and ByteDance both have subsidiaries in Ulanqab, but those subsidiaries do not invoice customers for cloud services and AI models. Alibaba Cloud lists the companies that invoice for its main products . None of them is a wholly owned Alibaba subsidiary in Ulanqab, and none is registered in Inner Mongolia. ByteDance registered three subsidiaries in the city in 2026, yet invoices for its cloud business, Volcano Engine , still come from a Beijing company.
In the same Economic Observer report, a local tax official said a data center generates most of its local tax during construction. Once a data center is operating, company headquarters sell most of its data services. What remains locally is mainly taxes on land and buildings and employees’ personal income tax. The number of employees is limited, however; a completed gigawatt-scale campus usually has only a few hundred operations staff .
Not much revenue stays where the data center is built. In 2025, Ulanqab’s computing industry paid 368 million yuan ($55 million) in tax , less than 5 percent of the city’s revenue. China Taxation News , the State Taxation Administration’s newspaper, reported that tax from the city’s computing industry rose more than 60 percent year-on-year in the first eight months of 2026. But construction has not stopped, so that increase cannot tell us what happens after the data centers open. When construction ends, construction-phase tax will recede. Taxes on land and buildings recur every year, but they depend on the site and the property, not on sales.
Liu Huansuo, deputy director of Ulanqab’s big data administration, told Xinhua : “If we rely solely on cheap electricity and low land costs, we risk becoming little more than ‘landlords of server rooms.’” That is a problem for Ulanqab’s finances.
In 2025, the city’s own revenue covered less than a fifth of its spending, and higher levels of government supplied more than half of its available funds. Those governments decide how much Ulanqab receives; the city decides for itself how to spend local tax revenue. Yet as data centers based in Ulanqab sell more and more cloud and AI services, the tax revenue goes to Hangzhou and Beijing. If Ulanqab is to “extend the industrial chain,” it will probably still need money from higher levels of government.
Some places in China do capture the tax on cloud services because the invoicing company is registered locally. Gui’an New Area in Guizhou is one of them. In the first 10 months of 2025, digital companies in Gui’an recorded 75.2 billion yuan ($11.2 billion) in invoiced sales , nearly 90 percent of it from 18 firms, including Huawei Cloud and Tencent. Huawei Cloud has announced that contracts and invoices for its customers in China will mainly be signed and issued by a company registered in Gui’an. Firms are willing to register an invoicing company in Gui’an, but they will not set one up everywhere they have a data center.
Alibaba and ByteDance can argue the profit comes from their models and customers, so paying the tax at headquarters is reasonable. That is a fair point, yet it leaves the host area in the lurch. Ulanqab can keep the tax paid during construction and the taxes on land and buildings, but neither will grow the way sales do to support sustainable development.
As the national “East Data, West Computing” program moves data centers west to power China’s AI push, other western places that host data centers face the same arithmetic – unless the invoicing companies register there. Ulanqab’s 109 signed data-center projects are expected to come online within two to three years. Once construction stops, the city’s tax take from computing may stop growing, and with it the chance to turn data centers into lasting development.

articles.title_orig: Apple Intelligence with Alibaba comes to China in December
articles.title_zh: Apple Intelligence with Alibaba comes to China in December
articles.content_orig:
After many months of discussion , Apple has figured out a way to bring Apple Intelligence to China, working with Alibaba’s Qwen model on some features. Apple Intelligence will soon be made available as a developer beta and will ship to Chinese customers in December with iOS 27.3.
China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology approved the use of Alibaba AI models with the iPhone in October 2026. Confirming the complexity of bringing these tools to China, Apple also received clearance in July from the Cyberspace Administration of China. Apple watchers are at liberty to reflect that the news comes at the best possible time for the company, which continues to grow smartphone market share in China.
The promise of integrated AI support in the form of Apple Intelligence can only boost interest in the company’s recently introduced iPhone Duo . Recent Counterpoint Research data claims iPhone sales increased 29% year on year in China in the three weeks following launch of the 18 Pro series devices. Initial stock of the devices sold out in hours.
China is also the world’s biggest market for foldable devices, which prompted some enterprising individuals to attempt to resell purchased iPhone Duos for far above their store price — scalpers have since reduced prices , because even in iPhone-crazy China, people weren’t willing to pay so much.
While it’s a big step for Apple AI in China, it’s not quite the great leap Apple may have wanted to put in place.
Siri AI is not supported and won’t be “anytime soon,” according to market speculation . While little is said about the reasons for that, it seems probable that political pressure in both the US and China may be partly to blame, as both nations see control of the means of AI production as essential for the future success of their differing ideologies. Apple has had to allow the Chinese government to approve ongoing updates to the suite.
Chinese users can use Alibaba’s Qwen in Siri, writing tools, and visual intelligence, including functions related to text and image understanding. They don’t get Image Playground, but can expect:
Apple and Alibaba also promise to maintain privacy. Customers will be able to choose if they wish to proceed with making a request through Qwen. Alibaba also said it would not use these requests for model training, though it isn’t yet clear if requests are going to Private Cloud Compute in Apple’s Chinese AI deployment.
Will the introduction of Apple Intelligence in China make a difference? It probably already is, as months of ever stronger speculation mean most Chinese consumers knew Apple AI was coming to their iPhones even as they purchased them before the announcement took place.
While the initial sales rush on Apple’s new devices among Chinese consumers has slowed, the news may help generate fresh enthusiasm for the iPhone in China. That’s great for Apple, but not such great news for some smaller smartphone vendors, who continue to be hammered by vicious increases in memory and other component prices.
Speaking almost two years ago when industry observers had anticipated an Apple Intelligence launch in China would take place earlier, Morgan Stanley then suggested the Alibaba partnership would be “a critical catalyst for Apple’s competitive standing in China.”
Other than painful price increases, not much has changed, and the introduction can only help consolidate the iPhone’s appeal in China. That’s good for Apple’s customers there, and great news for Apple’s investors everywhere else. It may even do something to retain a little US soft power.
In the background, we see the continued economic pressure wrought by fast-increasing memory prices. This has driven smartphone makers to raise prices, which has itself driven a 21% year on year decline in sector sales .
Apple and Samsung have proved more resilient to these price hikes than others, which means the added appeal generated by the launch of Apple Intelligence in the world’s second-largest economy is likely to make a highly significant difference to its market share in the short term, as well as shoring up share in future replacement cycles.

articles.title_zh: Cyberattacks hit supermarket fridges and freezers in Europe, Belgium launches investigation
articles.content_orig:
Dozens of supermarkets in Europe have reported temperatures of their refrigerators and fridges rising overnight, now widely believed to be caused by cyber attacks similar to the one that affected France several weeks ago.
Supermarket chains in Belgium, Sweden, Estonia, Netherlands, Luxembourg and Ireland have been affected.
The story began with Belgian media reporting on Monday that fridges were turned up to 17 degrees Celsius, forcing many stores to throw away food.
Belgium's Centre for Cybersecurity (CCB) told Belgian outlet Belga that it is aware of an incident targeting supermarket refrigeration systems.
CCB spokesperson Katrien Eggers told Euronews Next, "We are aware of an incident, but have no further information." There are no reports yet as to who was behind the attack... and it may never be possible to identify them."
Belgium's federal prosecutor's office have opened an investigation into the incident, according to a spokesperson.
Some 40 Delhaize Proxy supermarkets, 15 Carrefour Shop & Go stores, 15 Intermarché shops and five Spar Q8 service station locations have reportedly been impacted in Belgium, according to Belgian outlet Le Soir .
Butchery group De Laet en Van Haver also said that their fridges were affected. IKEA have also said their Bergen shop located at Mons was affected, bringing the total to 75 stores affected in Belgium.
"We have identified an IT incident affecting the refrigeration systems in several dozen stores. We immediately took the necessary measures to keep our stores operational," a spokesperson from Delhaize told Euronews Next.
Carrefour told Euronews Next this morning that "the impact at Carrefour is very limited: currently 15 of our 700 stores are affected, both in Flanders and Wallonia. Not a single hypermarket is among them."
"All stores remain open because it only concerns a few refrigeration units, mainly freezers. Quick action was taken so that all stores can stay open," they added.
Meanwhile later this morning Carrefour Belgium spokesman Mich Vergauwen said, "It's a cyberattack, there is no other reason," adding that the "impact is very limited".
It's believed the incident took place between Sunday night and Monday morning, skyrocketing refrigerator temperatures.
Stephan Moelans, CEO of refrigeration installer Sabcobel, which manages Delhaize's fridges and freeze systems, told the Belga news outlet that the Belgian attack involves exactly the same mechanism as the previous French cyberattack.
"Over the past few weeks, we've been working very hard to protect our customers' fridges against this vulnerability," Moelans said.
He said the incident happened when the units' evaporators were switched to defrost mode.
The refrigeration executive said a software update alone is not enough to address the vulnerability, with physical modifications required instead.
"That requires investment. The simplest solution is to manage the fridges over a secure internet connection. Most of our customers switched to that after the attack in France."
Sabcobel know of around twenty affected units, out of the hundreds it manages across Belgium.
Danfoss, the company that supplied the software for the refrigeration systems affected in both the latest incident and the one in France in October, said customers who had not updated their software were affected.
A spokesperson told VTM NIEUWS that "the company says that the vulnerability lies primarily in outdated software and that they had already urged customers to start using their new software".
Problems reportedly also occurred at a number of stores of the Swedish supermarket chains ICA and Coop last night, with refrigerators and freezers turned up to 50 degrees Celsius.
A similar incident occurred in Estonian at one location of supermarket chain Selver, according to media reports.
13 SuperValu stores in Ireland were affected by a suspected cyber incident, according to a statement by owner Musgrave made to the Irish Times.
In the Netherlands, the freezing and cooling systems of at least seventeen companies were attacked last night, according to a spokesperson for supplier Danfoss. The identities of the companies were not disclosed.
Delhaize also suspended its ordering systems in Luxembourg as a precaution to prevent a similar incident.
Finnish media report that several K Group supermarkets have been affected. K Group is one of Finland's largest retail chains.
These reported incidents follow a similar attack in France just weeks ago, on 12 October, when hundreds of French supermarkets belonging to the Intermarché and Coopérative U chains fell victim to a cyberattack targeting their refrigeration systems.
